events.title: Ahasuerus's Feast and Vashti's Fall
events.description: King Ahasuerus of Persia holds a magnificent banquet in the citadel of Susa that lasts for 180 days, followed by a seven-day celebration for all the people. When the king orders Queen Vashti to appear before the guests, she refuses. In his rage, the king consults with his wise men, and Vashti is deposed as queen to set an example for all women in the kingdom.

events.title: Esther Becomes Queen
events.description: A search is launched for a new queen among the young women of the kingdom. Mordecai, a Jewish man in Susa, has raised his cousin Hadassah, also called Esther. She is brought to the king's harem and wins favor with everyone. After twelve months of beautification, she is taken to the king, who loves her more than all the other women. He places the royal crown on her head and makes her queen in place of Vashti.

events.title: Mordecai Uncovers a Conspiracy
events.description: Mordecai sits at the king's gate and learns of a conspiracy against the king. Two of the king's officials, Bigthan and Teresh, plan to lay hands on King Ahasuerus. Mordecai informs Queen Esther, who reports it to the king in Mordecai's name. The matter is investigated and confirmed, and the two men are hanged. The event is recorded in the chronicles in the presence of the king.

events.title: Haman Is Promoted and Plans the Destruction of the Jews
events.description: The king promotes Haman the Agagite above all his princes. All at the king's gate bow down to Haman, but Mordecai refuses. Haman becomes furious and considers it too little to punish only Mordecai. He casts lots (pur) to find the best time and persuades the king to issue a decree to destroy all the Jews in the empire on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. Letters are sent to all provinces with the king's seal.

events.title: Mordecai Urges Esther to Act
events.description: Mordecai tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and ashes, and cries out loudly in the city. Esther hears of his distress and sends messengers to him. Mordecai tells her about the decree and urges her to go to the king to plead for mercy for her people. Esther hesitates because anyone who goes uninvited to the king risks death. Mordecai replies with the famous words: "Who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?" Esther asks Mordecai to gather all the Jews for three days of fasting.

events.title: Esther's Banquet
events.description: Esther puts on her royal robes and enters the inner court. The king extends his golden scepter toward her and offers to grant any request, up to half the kingdom. Esther asks only that the king and Haman come to a banquet she has prepared. At the banquet, the king again asks her to state her petition, but Esther invites them to another banquet the next day. Haman goes home happy, but becomes furious when he sees Mordecai at the gate. His wife Zeresh advises him to build a gallows for Mordecai.

events.title: Mordecai Honored by Haman
events.description: That night the king cannot sleep and orders the chronicles to be read aloud to him. He discovers that Mordecai was never rewarded for exposing the conspiracy. When Haman arrives to ask permission to hang Mordecai, the king asks him: "What should be done for the man the king wishes to honor?" Haman thinks the king means himself and suggests royal robes and a public procession through the city. To his horror, Haman is ordered to do exactly this for Mordecai.

events.title: Esther Reveals Haman's Plot
events.description: At the second banquet, the king again asks Esther what she wants. Esther reveals that she is a Jew and that she and her people have been sold for destruction. The king asks who is behind it, and Esther points to Haman as "the adversary and enemy." The king rises in anger and goes out into the garden.

events.title: Haman's Downfall and Execution
events.description: Haman throws himself at Esther's feet to beg for mercy, but the king interprets this as an assault on the queen. One of the officials mentions the gallows Haman built for Mordecai. The king orders that Haman himself be hanged on it, and thus the king's anger subsides.

events.title: The Jews' Victory and the Feast of Purim
events.description: The king gives Haman's house to Esther and elevates Mordecai. Since a royal decree cannot be revoked, the king issues a new letter granting the Jews the right to defend themselves. On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews strike down their enemies and take revenge. Esther requests an extra day in Susa. Mordecai establishes the festival of Purim, named after the lot (pur), as an annual celebration commemorating their deliverance.

events.title: Mordecai Elevated
events.description: King Ahasuerus imposes a tax throughout the empire. Mordecai the Jew becomes the second most powerful man in the kingdom after the king. He works for the good of his people and speaks for peace and prosperity for all his descendants. His greatness is recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.
